rendered:
NFA-A: after the high-rate step, when the C-rate was lowered, it recovered to a low-rate capacity of ≈170 mAh g^− 1[1], against an initial low-rate capacity, measured before the rate tests, of ≈184 mAh g^− 1[2]. The paper describes this as similar (≈5%)[3] to the initial capacity, so its stated loss for NFA-A is about the size given in that phrase.
NFA-F: after the same high-rate step, it recovered only to a low-rate capacity of ≈138 mAh g^− 1[4], against an initial low-rate capacity of ≈190 mAh g^− 1[5]. The paper gives its loss as ≈27% loss[6].
The paper concludes that NFA-A was the most stable of the variants under these test conditions. Note that the NFA-A capacities as printed imply a larger drop than the stated figure for NFA-A, so the paper's percentage does not exactly match its own numbers; the NFA-F capacities are consistent with its stated loss.
